records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be designed to have excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility for medical implants?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with various compositions, such as TiZrNbTa, HfNbTaTiZr, and TiZrHfNbTa. Test conditions: Tensile and compressive tests, fatigue tests, corrosion tests, and biocompatibility tests. Findings: The equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr achieves a tensile yield strength of 974 MPa and has an elongation of 20%; The O element doped TiZrHfNb exhibited a yield strength of 1,300 MPa and an elongation of 30% in the room temperature tensile test; HfNbTaTiZr exhibits good performance in fatigue tests, with a maximum stress required to exceed the yield stress causing fatigue failure; TiNbTaZrMo HEA exhibited excellent biocompatibility, with osteoblast density higher than that of SUS316L and CP-Ti; TiZrHfNbTa HEA has a corrosion rate of 10–4 mm/year under an environment of a low passive current density of approximately 10–2 A/m2. Mechanism: The excellent mechanical properties of HEAs are attributed to their unique composition and homogeneous microstructure, which leads to a variety of ingredients and complex microstructures. Limitations: The current research on bio-HEAs focuses on in vitro cell viability tests, lacking relevant in vivo animal experiments. Future work: Designing the bio-HEA composition and regulating the microstructure and morphology to obtain excellent bio-HEAs. Quote: "high freedom in element design"
